The complete archive

Three seasons.
Sixty-four conversations.

Every episode of Slow Burn Stories, grouped by season, newest first. Roughly 67 hours of recording in total. Some are longer than they should be. None are shorter than they want to be.

Season All Season 3 Season 2 Season 1

Season 3

Spring–Summer 2026 · in progress · 14 episodes so far
  1. 14S3
    Building a tool library from a single donated drill with Marcus Haines · Foundry Row Four years of slow, deliberate growing — and the single suggestion that turned a tool-share into something closer to a neighborhood institution.
    1:12:14 Jun 17
  2. 13S3
    The neighborhood watch that became a mutual aid network with Renata Okonkwo-Lima · East Boston Resilience Hub It started with a phone tree during a blackout. Five years later they run a pantry, a tool share, and a monthly repair clinic.
    1:06:48 Jun 10
  3. 12S3
    A small press, a single typeface, and twelve books a year with Junie Coltrane · Quailfeather Editions Junie publishes literature in translation from a converted laundry room in Providence. She sets every book in the same revival of Janson.
    1:18:02 Jun 3
  4. 11S3
    What eighteen years of beekeeping taught me about risk with Annette Wei · second-generation apiarist On colony collapse, family inheritance, and what it means to share weather data with twelve other Sonoma County beekeepers over coffee.
    1:08:31 May 27
  5. 10S3
    Twenty years of weather data, kept by hand with Esme Tarkanian · phenology researcher Fifty-seven notebooks. One acre. A long conversation about who gets to claim a record once it leaves the kitchen table.
    1:11:55 May 20
  6. 09S3
    Running a 14-seat restaurant for thirty-one years with Frank Beaumont-Pasco · chef-owner, Casita Bira The same menu, with seasonal substitutions, since 1993. A six-month waitlist. Never advertised. Stubbornly, beautifully ordinary.
    1:21:09 May 13
  7. 08S3
    The cooperative bookstore that survived a chain opening across the street with Priya Bandyopadhyay-Hale · The Foxglove Collective Priya walks me through fifteen years of decisions, the worst of which was switching their POS in 2019. What worked: a stubborn refusal to discount.
    1:09:22 May 6
  8. 07S3
    The economist who quit to make hand-thrown teacups with Hideo Maruyama · potter Eleven years at the World Bank, then a wheel and a kiln in his basement. He still thinks he is, in some real sense, doing economics.
    1:14:11 Apr 15
  9. 06S3
    A free legal clinic that won't take grant money with Asha Voloshin-Reyes · founder, Open Door Legal Asha runs a tenants' rights clinic in Vallejo entirely on small-dollar donations. We argue, gently, about the cost of independence.
    1:05:44 Apr 8
  10. 05S3
    Teaching kids to weld in a town with no shop class with Ramona Estill · founder, Ironwood Skills Project Ramona started teaching welding to high schoolers in a Humboldt County warehouse after the district cut industrial arts. We talk about insurance, parents, and the smell of flux.
    1:16:38 Apr 1
  11. 04S3
    The newsletter that pays its writers more than it pays the founder with Jonas Krieger-Adebayo · The Slow Wire Jonas runs a longform climate newsletter with seventeen contributors and one rule. He explains the rule. It's a hard rule.
    1:03:58 Mar 25
  12. 03S3
    A community radio station that broadcasts in four languages with Liana Acquaviva-Brennan · KHZR 88.3 Liana inherited a sleepy FM signal in Salinas and turned it into the only Spanish, Mixtec, Tagalog, and Hmong news source in the valley.
    1:10:27 Mar 18
  13. 02S3
    A seed library run out of the back of a bicycle shop with Wren Halverson · Common Roots Seed Co-op Wren stores 1,400 varieties in repurposed library card-catalog drawers. The catalog itself was donated by a retired librarian named Marge. We talk about Marge.
    1:07:12 Mar 11
  14. 01S3
    Season Three: a year of building things slowly on purpose with Cassia Romero · host introduction A short solo opener — what I'm hoping to do this season, who I've already recorded with, and the listener question that finally changed the format.
    22:48 Mar 4

Season 2

Fall 2024 – Winter 2025 · 24 episodes · complete
  1. 24S2
    A season finale — and what I learned reading every listener email with Cassia Romero · solo A 38-minute closer on the year, the show, and a slightly tearful thank-you to the four people who helped me move studios in October.
    38:14 Feb 18
  2. 23S2
    The luthier rebuilding pre-war Gibsons one bridge at a time with Toral Brimhall-Okafor · independent repair Toral works out of a former butcher shop in Lawrence, Kansas. We talk about hide glue, hairline cracks, and why she's stopped advertising entirely.
    1:17:33 Feb 11
  3. 22S2
    A worker-owned bakery in its eighth year with Sage Mendelsohn-Park · Common Loaf Bakery Co-op Five members, three ovens, one very long argument about whether to serve coffee. Sage walks me through the bylaws.
    1:13:09 Feb 4
  4. 21S2
    Building a free clinic in a converted laundromat with Dr. Imani Sutton-Vázquez · nurse practitioner Imani runs a sliding-scale primary care clinic in San Pablo with three volunteer providers. The dryer hookups now hold their vaccine fridge.
    1:05:21 Jan 28
  5. 20S2
    The youth orchestra in a town of nine hundred with Beatrix Hollander-Quinn · music director Bea conducts a 28-piece string ensemble in Trinity County. Most of her musicians are her former students. Most of the instruments she's repaired herself.
    1:01:48 Jan 21
  6. 19S2
    A printmaker who hand-cranks every poster with Kofi Underwood-Mensah · Crane Press Kofi has run a single-color screenprint shop in Pittsburgh since 2011. The cylinder press he uses was rescued from a flooded basement.
    1:09:55 Jan 21
  7. 18S2
    The library that decided to stop asking people to be quiet with Devon Asante-Klein · branch librarian Five years after Devon's branch dropped its silence policy, cardholder waitlists have tripled. We talk about who libraries are actually for.
    1:09:33 Jan 14
  8. 17S2
    A bike shop that does free repairs on Wednesdays — forever with Yuki Saint-Hilaire · Half-Step Cycles Yuki's shop has run a no-cost Wednesday repair night since 2017. We talk about boundaries, regulars, and one customer named Carl.
    58:14 Jan 7
  9. 16S2
    The slow-fashion label that releases two pieces a year with Mireille Tannenbaum-Cho · Aphelion Studio Mireille designs, drafts, sources, and personally hand-finishes two garments annually. There is, somehow, a waitlist.
    1:12:42 Dec 17
  10. 15S2
    An astronomer who runs a public telescope every Friday night with Dr. Aldric Petrov-Sandhu · Mount Hamilton volunteer Aldric has manned the Lick Observatory's small public scope every Friday for twenty-six years. We talk about clouds, kids, and patience as a discipline.
    1:04:17 Dec 10
  11. 14S2
    Founding a doula collective in a maternity desert with Calliope Mwangi-Ferreira · The Birthroom Cal trained twenty-three doulas across three rural counties after the local hospital closed its L&D ward. The collective now attends 300 births a year.
    1:18:55 Dec 3
  12. 13S2
    A research garden devoted entirely to one genus of tomato with Idris Vannucci-Lloyd · Solanum Project Idris grows 217 varieties of wild and heirloom tomato in a Sebastopol greenhouse. He gives the seeds away. He has thoughts about why.
    1:11:08 Nov 26
  13. 12S2
    A tutoring program in a juvenile hall, run by formerly incarcerated teachers with Theodora "Teddy" Onuoha-Pratt · Open Page Teddy runs a writing program at Alameda County's juvenile facility. Everyone on her teaching team has been inside themselves. We talk about what that changes.
    1:21:48 Nov 19

Season 1

Spring–Summer 2024 · 26 episodes · complete
  1. 26S1
    A season finale, a year in, and a thank you with Cassia Romero · solo closer The first season finale — what worked, what didn't, and the eleven listeners who showed up to my first live recording in Berkeley.
    41:22 Aug 27
  2. 22S1
    A pickle company that started in a basement with Wallace Kim-Donnelly · Stone & Brine Wallace ferments cucumbers in repurposed sauerkraut crocks and ships to fourteen states. The original basement is now a small warehouse next to the basement.
    1:04:18 Jul 30
  3. 18S1
    An archivist who digitizes one family album at a time, for free with Florencia "Flor" Pereira-Stowe · The Kitchen Table Archive Flor runs a slow, careful family-photo digitization project from her apartment in Long Beach. She has a four-year waitlist.
    1:14:55 Jul 2
  4. 12S1
    A storm-chasing climatologist who runs a free SMS alert network with Dr. Lior Halberstam-Quintero · NowCast Plains Lior texts hyperlocal tornado warnings to 11,000 Kansans. The whole operation runs on a six-year-old laptop. He calls it the most expensive cheap thing he's ever done.
    1:08:22 May 21
  5. 06S1
    A naturalist who has walked the same trail every morning for thirty years with Bertram "Bert" Solana-Whittaker · Tilden Park Bert keeps a notebook. He notices when the manzanita blooms two days later than usual. We talk about why no one else seems to.
    1:01:14 Apr 9
  6. 01S1
    Episode one: a magazine editor leaves her job and buys a microphone with Cassia Romero · solo introduction The first-ever episode. Why I left, what I'm hoping to do, and a quiet thank-you to my sister Inez who lent me the down payment on the microphone.
    28:11 Mar 5
